name: combine_styles
title: Combine two or more ANSI styles

origin.description: Combine styles into one function. They are applied from right to left.

arguments.text: Style functions or names from styles().

arguments.name: crayon
arguments.text: A style function, on the left of $.

arguments.name: style
arguments.text: A name in styles(), on the right of $.

origin.details: Two foreground colors, or two background colors, fight: the outer one wins because it is applied later. $ looks the name up in styles() and appends that style. The original style function is left unchanged.
origin.example:
alert <- bold $ red $ bgCyan
cat(alert("Warning!"), "\n", sep="")

translation.description: Combine styles into one function. They are applied from right to left.

arguments.name: name
arguments.text: An attribute, the style name used on the right of $.

translation.details: bold.red.bgCyan is bold $ red $ bgCyan. The right-most style is the inner one. Combining does not change the style it started from.
